analysis.title: Flows & Liquidity: An overhang of long duration and spread exposures
key_insights: Bond positioning is bifurcated. Quant funds such as CTAs have profited from building short duration exposures over the past month, while discretionary managers are scrambling to reduce earlier overhangs of long duration and spread exposures.

This creates two-way risk for bonds. Either mean reversion signals trigger quant profit taking and reverse part of the recent rise in yields, or discretionary managers cut duration and spread exposure further and amplify the negative momentum. JPM's bias is the latter in the near term because discretionary bond managers are larger than quant managers.

Provisional September hedge fund data show quant funds returned roughly 3%-4% on the month by exploiting the bond selloff and tech stock gyrations. Equity Long/Short and Discretionary Macro were slightly down or flat. Event Driven, Credit and Equity Sector funds were down.

CTA momentum signals for UST and Bund futures reached extreme territory on September 30th. This creates a risk of profit taking and mean reversion into Q4 and leaves Managed Futures/CTA funds vulnerable to a bond market reversal.

Evidence of discretionary long duration overhang: US and Euro active bond mutual fund betas have caught up with elevated total duration, balanced mutual funds held above-average bond exposure and have been retreating, and the Treasury and European client surveys show a persistent long duration overhang and intra-EMU spread exposure among real money managers.
Risk parity funds hold below-average leverage and have capacity to add bond exposure, but have been reluctant to do so given higher bond volatility.
Futures position proxies for 10y USTs, Bunds and OATs fell into end-September, which JPM attributes to discretionary managers cutting duration and spread exposure.

FX reserve managers saw net inflows of about $80bn in 2Q26 after about $16bn in 1Q26. Dollar reserves had modest outflows of about $15bn in 2Q, reversing part of the $42bn inflow in 1Q. Euro reserves took in about $100bn and yen reserves lost just over $40bn. JPM reads this as a partial resumption of reserve diversification that paused in 1Q when central banks preferred liquidity at the start of the Middle East conflict.
The dollar share of FX reserves ex gold is projected to fall further to about 56.3% in 3Q26 based on FX and bond returns.

Central bank gold purchases rebounded to nearly 290 tonnes in 2Q26 (just over $40bn) from about 56 tonnes in 1Q26. The gold share of total central bank reserves fell from about 31% to just under 28% in 2Q on valuation effects and is projected to be just above 28% in 3Q.

Modest inflows into FX reserves since the first half of 2025 have not reversed the downward trend in FX reserves relative to global GDP. JPM keeps its conclusion that the reserve-recycling pillar of the 'savings glut' remains weak or has shifted to SWFs and private vehicles that are more price sensitive and less fixed income focused.

After Brazil's first-round presidential election, CME Ibovespa futures positioning showed little buying, while BRL futures positioning (uptrending since April 2025) and EWZ ETF flows rose. JPM reads retail as more optimistic on Brazilian equities than institutions, since EWZ short interest, which is more institution-driven, was only slightly lower.

YTD EM equity and bond fund flows are the best since 2021 ahead of the Brazil election. EEM and EMB saw little inflow after the election and little change in short interest. EEM short interest has declined this year and recently went below EMB's for the first time since the pandemic, so EM bonds look less vulnerable than EM equities from a short interest view.

Overall capital flow into digital assets is about $50bn YTD, an annualized pace of $66bn. That is above the $52bn annualized pace as of last May but about half of last year's pace. The estimate now includes private corporate treasuries, private miners and government-related entities.

Crypto flows in 1H26 were driven by MicroStrategy purchases and crypto VC funding while ETF flows were a headwind, with heavy outflows in May and June. ETF flows have improved since August and are net positive for the year, but cumulative flows since the October 10th 2025 downturn are still net negative.

CME futures proxies show bitcoin positioning above its prior peak and ethereum positioning near its October 2025 high. Offshore perpetual futures leverage proxies are off peak but above historical averages. CTA momentum signals show rebuilding of long positions in bitcoin and ethereum.
In Q3 both crypto ETF flows and futures positioning rose, pointing to greater retail and institutional participation and positive flow momentum into Q4.

Crypto VC funding has improved since 2024 but is concentrated in fewer, larger rounds led by established firms, shifting from equity toward debt financing of infrastructure businesses. Tokenization is gaining traction in B2B VC funding.

Bitcoin miners are net sellers YTD at roughly $1.8bn, mostly public miners selling newly mined coins or drawing down holdings to fund AI infrastructure capex. Public corporate treasuries have shifted funding from debt toward preferred shares, which raises interest and dividend payment needs.

Appendix vol monitor: 3m 10y US swap implied vol is at 108%, its 1y high on 5 Oct 2026. 10y Euro swap vol is at 98%, near its high of 99%. S&P 500 implied vol is 14%, at its 1y low area. CDX IG and CDX HY implied vol run at 2.19x and 2.13x realized.
Appendix bitcoin monitor: current production cost is about $85k against a market price of about $83k.

Public bitcoin miners selling holdings and corporate treasuries needing to service preferred dividends and debt could weigh on crypto flows.

vol_and_positioning: Managed Futures/CTA momentum signals in UST and Bund futures hit extreme short-duration territory on September 30th, raising mean reversion and profit-taking risk into Q4.

Quant funds returned 3%-4% in September while discretionary funds were flat or down. Managed Futures/CTAs are +14.34% YTD and Macro Quant +11.27% YTD, against Equity L/S +7.44% and Discretionary Macro +4.11%.
Risk parity implied leverage is below average, leaving capacity to add bonds, but funds have held back because of higher bond volatility.

3m ATM implied vol: S&P 500 14% (1y low 14%, implied/realized 1.30x), 10y US swaps 108% (1y high set 5 Oct, 1.56x), 10y Euro swaps 98% (1y high 99% on 2 Oct, 1.36x), CDX IG 44% (2.19x), CDX HY 42% (2.13x), Brent 46% (1.05x), Gold 21% (1.21x).
EEM short interest has fallen below EMB short interest for the first time since the pandemic.
TMT-focused equity sector hedge funds returned 2.19% in September and 21.83% Jan-Sep 2026, after -8.29% in July.
geopolitical: Central banks preferred liquidity at the onset of the Middle East conflict in 1Q26, pausing reserve diversification flows.
Brazil's first-round presidential election shaped institutional versus retail positioning in Brazilian assets.

tension_points.bull_case: Quant funds' extreme short-duration positions mean-revert and they take profit, reversing part of the recent rise in bond yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary managers keep cutting their long duration and spread overhang, which amplifies the negative momentum in bonds. JPM's bias is this outcome in the near term because discretionary managers are larger than quant managers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Mean reversion signals kicking in and inducing CTAs to take profit from their extreme short duration positions.

theme_stances.key_argument: Discretionary managers are likely to keep cutting long duration and spread exposure given their greater size versus quant managers.
theme_stances.evidence: Our bias is for the latter in the near term

theme_stances.key_argument: Modest dollar reserve outflows against a weaker broad dollar and overall reserve inflows suggest diversification flows partly resumed.
theme_stances.evidence: suggests some resumption of the diversification flow

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising ETF flows and futures positioning in Q3 point to broader retail and institutional participation.
theme_stances.evidence: thus creating a positive flow momentum into Q4
